chunks: Agent Desktop is a web-based application that enables agents to communicate with customers across multiple channels such as voice, chat, audio, video, social media and email. It provides 360-degree view of the customer journey and helps agents manage customer interactions across different touchpoints. It integrates to existing telephony such as Cisco, Avaya, AWS, and SIP with the minimal requirement. With an easy-to-use interface and a unified information repository, empowers the agents to interact with customers efficiently and effectively.

Multiple widgets are used to display interaction-related data. Enhanced voice functionality that supports easy transfer/conference of calls to other agents. Readymade themes to customize the desktop based on the agent’s preferences. Easy-to-use call controls to handle customer interactions effectively. Dedicated widget that displays customer details once the call is accepted. Detailed information provided on all past interactions that the customer has had with the contact center vis Customer Journey widget. Easy creation of event/task reminders.

This guide is intended for the following audience: Contact center agents who use the TMAC Agent Desktop to provide customer service over different media channels. Contact center supervisors who monitor and manage their team of agents.

The Agent Desktop is designed using widgets that provides a way to seamlessly manage distribution of information to or from the agent desktop, eliminating the need to open another application. You can personalize your desktop by adding, removing, repositioning the widgets based on your requirements.

The event polling mechanism in CIS is related to the Command Cache, in that it polls the content server on a scheduled interval and if changes are found, it sends out events through the CIS layer. These events tell the Command Cache that content has been updated, a subject has changed, etc., and to clear the cache appropriately. If the event poller is not enabled (via the Event Polling Properties tab on the adapter configuration page), then no events will be generated, and the cached items will only be expired via their timeout values. Agent Desktop (AD) is being upgraded to include support for social media channels like Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook. Comments from customers on these platforms—such as those on Facebook Business Posts, Twitter Business Tweets, and Instagram Business Posts—will be routed to available agents on the AD. Agents will be able to view and respond to these comments directly through the AD interface, facilitating prompt and effective communication with customers across social media channels.

When a customer comments or replies on business posts made on Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter, the details of these comments, including information about the post, will be automatically added as interactions within the "Social Media" tab of the Workbench. This applies only to posts from monitored business accounts on the specified social media platforms. Posts created by the business itself will not be routed to the Agent Desktop (AD). Only customer comments and replies on these business posts will be directed to the AD.

Social Media Interactions will be organized by channels—Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. Within each channel, interactions will be categorized by skill sets. Each interaction will show the account name of the customer who commented, along with the text of their comment or reply. Clicking on an interaction will reveal details about the post, including the total number of reactions and comments associated with it. Comments or replies related to the selected interaction will be highlighted. The Social Media tab in the Workbench will include the following sections: Queued: Contains all unassigned social media interactions. Inbox: Includes both assigned and unassigned social media interactions. Sent: Displays sent social media interactions. Drafts: Contains drafted social media interactions. Additionally, there will be a Post section displaying social media posts from Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. This section will include all posts and their related comments, replies, and reactions created till date for a monitored page,
in view-only mode. The purpose of this tab is to showcase posts with or without active interactions.

Agents can take the following actions on social media interactions in workbench: Pull Interaction - Pull the current interaction to respond to the post comment. Pulled interaction will be assigned to agent and will be displayed in Social Media Interaction tab. Transfer Interaction - Forward the interaction to another agent. Close Interaction - Close Interaction without responding to customer comments.

When actions such as editing, deleting posts or their comments and replies, or reacting to post comments or replies occur on social media platforms for interactions already active in the social media tab, the Agent Desktop will reflect these changes as follows: Edit Posts on Social Media Platform When a post on social media is edited, the popup message – ‘Post has been edited! ‘will be displayed for current interaction. A notification will also be sent to agents in AD. Next, edited posts will be refreshed in social media posts widgets in social media interaction tab. Clicking the notification will take agents to the Posts section of the Workbench, where the recently edited post will be highlighted and displayed. The Edit Icon will be updated to reflect the changes, and the previous contents of the post will not be shown. Edit comments or replies on Social Media Platform When a

comment or reply is edited on social media platform, the popup message – ‘Comment has been edited! ‘will be displayed for current interaction. A notification will also be sent to agents in AD. Next, edited customer comments will be updated in the Social Media Posts widget within the Social Media Interaction tab, marked with an "Edited" icon. Clicking the ‘i’ icon will display the most recent version of the comment or reply that was last edited. This information will appear only once and will disappear when you move to other interactions. the Posts section of the Workbench, where the currently deleted post will be highlighted and displayed. Social Media Posts widget will initially be in restored mode by default. Agents can switch it to maximized mode or floating window mode. Social Media Interactions will be categorized by channel (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter) and displayed to agents. For each interaction, the following details will be shown to the agent: Post Details: Includes the post contents, total post reactions, total post comments, active comment, active comment reactions (if any) and a section for the agent to reply. Agent Actions: Send Agent Replies for customer comments from AD and will be posted in social media platform. Save to Draft . Clear Agent Replies. Close current interaction without responding. interaction. Agents can view all comments/replies on the post and can return to the current comment by scrolling back or clicking on the 'Active' link located before Total Post Comments. Media files (photos, videos, GIFs, etc.) from customer comments will not be preloaded. An icon will be shown and on clicking this icon, media will be downloaded and shown in agent desktop.

Agent can perform below actions – Send Replies to Customer Comments: Agents can use text, images, videos, GIFs and emojis in their replies from AD. Agents can reply to the current customer’s comment and click on "Send Comments". The agent's comment will be posted on social media as a reply to the customer’s comment. After the agent sends a reply, the interaction will be closed. Both customer and agent comments can be viewed in the Sent Items section of the Workbench. Post Admin can edit an agent’s reply directly from social media (in case of any mistakes, errors, or incorrect information in the previously posted comment from AD). When an edit is made on social media on agent’s reply, a notification will be sent to agents in AD. Clicking on the notification will redirect them to the Sent Items section of the Workbench, where the current edited comments along with

the post will be displayed. Save to Draft: Agents can save replies as drafts to be sent later. To draft a reply, agents must click this button; replies will not be auto drafted. Agents can retrieve drafted replies from the Draft section of the Workbench. Clear Data: Agents can clear replies by clicking this button. On some days, you may have to check with your customers if the issue they have had has been resolved. And, on other days, you may require additional information from the customer to troubleshoot a problem, and your customers might ask you to reach out to them at a specific time. To handle such scenarios, TMAC supports creating reminders that enable you to perform your job efficiently. TMAC also supports creating task reminders where the system automatically performs the task at a specified time. For example, you can set a task reminder to change your status to Break at 3 PM on July 4th, 2021, or you can set a task reminder to launch an online meeting at 6 PM on July 6th, 2021. At the designated time, depending on the action configured, the system automatically performs the task (change status to break or launch an online meeting)

Event reminders are useful to remind you of any action that you must complete such as emailing a customer, attending a training session, troubleshooting a technical problem, etc at a specific day and time. To set event reminders, do the following: Click displayed on the calendar. Enter event title. Set the date from the calendar Set the time for the event. Enter location. Enter any additional notes. Click Add. The reminder is created, and it is displayed on the calendar (as a red bar). Note: You can edit the reminder by clicking the edit icon on the red bar before the expiry of the reminder date/time. You can also delete the reminder by clicking the delete icon. At the configured date and time, a pop-up window appears to remind you of the event. You can either click to accept the reminder or click the snooze button to set an interval
to bring back the reminder.

Task reminders are useful to automate tasks such as changing status, launching online meeting at a specific day and time. To set task reminders, do the following: Click displayed on the calendar Choose Tasks. Select the task from the drop-down. If you choose Call Customer, then enter the number of the customer you want to call. If you choose the Change Status task, then select the status you want to change to from the Select Status drop-down. If you choose Meeting task, then enter the meeting link. Set the date from the calendar Set the time for the task reminder. Enter location. Enter any additional notes. Click Add. The reminder is created, and it is displayed on the calendar (as a red bar). Note: You can edit the reminder by clicking the edit icon on the red bar before the expiry of the reminder date/time. You can also delete the

reminder by clicking the delete icon. At the configured date and time, a pop-up window appears to remind you of the task reminder. You can either click to accept the reminder or click the snooze button to set an interval to bring back the reminder. On accepting Call Customer task reminder, your status is changed to On Call and a call is made to the customer. On accepting the Change Status task reminder, your status is automatically changed by the system. On accepting the Meeting task reminder, an online meeting is launched by the system.

meta.text: Agent Desktop is a web-based application that enables agents to communicate with customers across multiple channels such as voice, chat, audio, video, social media and email. It provides 360-degree view of the customer journey and helps agents manage customer interactions across different touchpoints. It integrates to existing telephony such as Cisco, Avaya, AWS, and SIP with the minimal requirement. With an easy-to-use interface and a unified information repository, empowers the agents to interact with customers efficiently and effectively.

Multiple widgets are used to display interaction-related data. Enhanced voice functionality that supports easy transfer/conference of calls to other agents. Readymade themes to customize the desktop based on the agent’s preferences. Easy-to-use call controls to handle customer interactions effectively. Dedicated widget that displays customer details once the call is accepted. Detailed information provided on all past interactions that the customer has had with the contact center vis Customer Journey widget. Easy creation of event/task reminders.

This guide is intended for the following audience: Contact center agents who use the TMAC Agent Desktop to provide customer service over different media channels. Contact center supervisors who monitor and manage their team of agents.

The Agent Desktop is designed using widgets that provides a way to seamlessly manage distribution of information to or from the agent desktop, eliminating the need to open another application. You can personalize your desktop by adding, removing, repositioning the widgets based on your requirements.

For a new agent, the supervisor must configure the agent settings in the Omni Channel Manager (OCM) before the agent can start working on the desktop. To configure a new agent, do the following: Log in to OCM. Select TMAC >User Onboarding Enter details for the new agent. Select TMAC > Agent Skill Settings. Assign one or more skills to the agent. Note: For detailed information on OCM Administration, refer Tetherfi Omni Channel Manager Admin Module User Guide

AD is a web-based application that can be launched from any supported web browser such as Chrome, Firefox, Microsoft Edge (Windows 7) and Safari. To log in to the AD, do the following: Open your web browser and enter your contact center’s URL. URL Format: https://<domain_name>:<port>/<server_name> Enter your LDAP ID. Enter your LDAP password. Enter your station ID. Click Log In. On successful login, the home page is displayed. This is the login page used by the Agent to login to AD First Page seen by the Agent. Agent can login to the Agent Desktop’s main dashboard from here. Below are the features that can be seen in this page: Login: This is where user can login with just his lanid / stationid Auto login: This is where the user is auto logged in as soon as AD is loaded. This can be done by providing query parameters to the

login path. The following patterns of query parameters are accepted: lanid: This is used to pass the user’s lanid automatically without filling in the lanid field manually Stationid: This is used to pass the station id the user wants to log into automatically without filling in the field manually PBX: This is used to use enable PBX on login and values ‘1’ or ‘true’ can be passed to enable this on login If User attempts to click the LOGIN button without any credentials placed, an error message will appear stating, “LAN ID Not Provided” If user Toggles the “Login to PBX?” or “Login to Web phone” button, User must manually input the station as it’s a Required Field. If the agent is using the Avaya Hard Phone (IP Phone), they can log into Agent Desktop by enabling the "Log into PBX" option and providing their station ID If the agent
is using Web Phone, they can log into Agent Desktop by enabling the "Log into Web Phone" option and providing their station ID.

This is a dashboard with the business of AD as a product. This is where the agent spends his time communicating with the customers. Since this is generated dynamically, the content differs from customer to customer

This is where all the dynamic widgets of AD are created, configured, and maintained. The widgets are divided into different types and sub-types. The first division of the widgets can be based on the separation of the webpage. They can be shown as below: The Red box shows the “Toolbar” widgets. The yellow indicates the “Navbar” widgets. The blue section indicates the “Content” widgets. The purple box indicates the “AOT” (Always on top) widgets.

As discussed in the T-Widgets section, on a high-level view, the widgets can be divided into Toolbar, Navbar, Content and AOT widgets. In this section, we will see how Navbar, and Content widgets are further divided into different sub-types.

The Red box shows the “Toolbar” widgets. Toolbar widget is displayed at the top. There are different options displayed in the toolbar. The event polling mechanism in CIS is related to the Command Cache, in that it polls the content server on a scheduled interval and if changes are found, it sends out events through the CIS layer. These events tell the Command Cache that content has been updated, a subject has changed, etc., and to clear the cache appropriately. If the event poller is not enabled (via the Event Polling Properties tab on the adapter configuration page), then no events will be generated, and the cached items will only be expired via their timeout values. The Content widgets are further divided into different kinds of subtypes. This will be explained below. But before going into the classifications, it’s important to understand how the widgets are displayed. As shown above, AD’s “Content” part is divided into grids. These grids are divided into a total of 6x3 different sections, and the width of each widget is based on this grid dimensions. For example: The Wallboard widget size is 2x3, meaning it consumes 2 grids along the x-axis and 3 grids along the y-axis. The All-Interaction widget size is 1x1, meaning it consumes 1 grid across both the x and y-axes. The Interaction Details widget size is 2x1 meaning it consumes 2 grids along the x-axis and 1 grid along the y-axis. Now that the widget’s construction size is cleared, we can move on to the classifications of the Widgets.

Since this was a common pattern, and during interaction, some of the widgets must be displayed mandatorily, for example in the email interaction above, the “Email Controls” widget is an absolute must, Chat, Voice interactions also have a similar condition. To make this a more generalized pattern across AD, we have Static and Dynamic widgets. Agent Desktop (AD) is being upgraded to include support for social media channels like Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook. Comments from customers on these platforms—such as those on Facebook Business Posts, Twitter Business Tweets, and Instagram Business Posts—will be routed to available agents on the AD. Agents will be able to view and respond to these comments directly through the AD interface, facilitating prompt and effective communication with customers across social media channels.

When a customer comments or replies on business posts made on Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter, the details of these comments, including information about the post, will be automatically added as interactions within the "Social Media" tab of the Workbench. This applies only to posts from monitored business accounts on the specified social media platforms. Posts created by the business itself will not be routed to the Agent Desktop (AD). Only customer comments and replies on these business posts will be directed to the AD.

Social Media Interactions will be organized by channels—Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. Within each channel, interactions will be categorized by skill sets. Each interaction will show the account name of the customer who commented, along with the text of their comment or reply. Clicking on an interaction will reveal details about the post, including the total number of reactions and comments associated with it. Comments or replies related to the selected interaction will be highlighted. The Social Media tab in the Workbench will include the following sections: Queued: Contains all unassigned social media interactions. Inbox: Includes both assigned and unassigned social media interactions. Sent: Displays sent social media interactions. Drafts: Contains drafted social media interactions. Additionally, there will be a Post section displaying social media posts from Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. This section will include all posts and their related comments, replies, and reactions created till date for a monitored page,
in view-only mode. The purpose of this tab is to showcase posts with or without active interactions.

Agents can take the following actions on social media interactions in workbench: Pull Interaction - Pull the current interaction to respond to the post comment. Pulled interaction will be assigned to agent and will be displayed in Social Media Interaction tab. Transfer Interaction - Forward the interaction to another agent. Close Interaction - Close Interaction without responding to customer comments.

When actions such as editing, deleting posts or their comments and replies, or reacting to post comments or replies occur on social media platforms for interactions already active in the social media tab, the Agent Desktop will reflect these changes as follows: Edit Posts on Social Media Platform When a post on social media is edited, the popup message – ‘Post has been edited! ‘will be displayed for current interaction. A notification will also be sent to agents in AD. Next, edited posts will be refreshed in social media posts widgets in social media interaction tab. Clicking the notification will take agents to the Posts section of the Workbench, where the recently edited post will be highlighted and displayed. The Edit Icon will be updated to reflect the changes, and the previous contents of the post will not be shown. Edit comments or replies on Social Media Platform When a

comment or reply is edited on social media platform, the popup message – ‘Comment has been edited! ‘will be displayed for current interaction. A notification will also be sent to agents in AD. Next, edited customer comments will be updated in the Social Media Posts widget within the Social Media Interaction tab, marked with an "Edited" icon. Clicking the ‘i’ icon will display the most recent version of the comment or reply that was last edited. This information will appear only once and will disappear when you move to other interactions. Delete Posts on Social Media Platform When a post is deleted on social media platform, the popup message – ‘Post has been deleted! This interaction will be closed. ‘will be displayed for current interaction. A notification will also be sent to agents in AD. On clicking ‘Ok’ button, interaction will be closed. Clicking the notification will take agents to

the Posts section of the Workbench, where the currently deleted post will be highlighted and displayed. Posts and comments will remain in the Workbench, but a Deleted Icon will appear for the post across all sections (Queue, Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Posts). Actions such as Transfer, Pull, and Close will be disabled for these posts. Delete comment or replies on Social Media Platform When a post comments/replies are deleted on social media platform, the popup message – ‘Comment has been deleted! This interaction will be closed. ‘will be displayed for current interaction. A notification will also be sent to agents in AD. On clicking ‘Ok’ button, interaction will be closed. licking the notification will direct agents to the Inbox section of the Workbench, where the currently deleted comment or reply will be highlighted and displayed. Comments will not be removed from the Workbench. A Deleted Icon will appear for the comment
across all sections (Queue, Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Posts) in the Workbench. Actions such as Transfer, Pull, and Close will be disabled for these comments.

Agent Actions: Send Agent Replies for customer comments from AD and will be posted in social media platform. Save to Draft . Clear Agent Replies. Close current interaction without responding. Agent can perform below actions – Send Replies to Customer Comments: Agents can use text, images, videos, GIFs and emojis in their replies from AD. On some days, you may have to check with your customers if the issue they have had has been resolved. And, on other days, you may require additional information from the customer to troubleshoot a problem, and your customers might ask you to reach out to them at a specific time. To handle such scenarios, TMAC supports creating reminders that enable you to perform your job efficiently. TMAC also supports creating task reminders where the system automatically performs the task at a specified time. For example, you can set a task reminder to change your status to Break at 3 PM on July 4th, 2021, or you can set a task reminder to launch an online meeting at 6 PM on July 6th, 2021. At the designated time, depending on the action configured, the system automatically performs the task (change status to break or launch an online meeting)

Event reminders are useful to remind you of any action that you must complete such as emailing a customer, attending a training session, troubleshooting a technical problem, etc at a specific day and time. To set event reminders, do the following: Click displayed on the calendar. Enter event title. Set the date from the calendar Set the time for the event. Enter location. Enter any additional notes. Click Add. The reminder is created, and it is displayed on the calendar (as a red bar). Note: You can edit the reminder by clicking the edit icon on the red bar before the expiry of the reminder date/time. You can also delete the reminder by clicking the delete icon. At the configured date and time, a pop-up window appears to remind you of the event. You can either click to accept the reminder or click the snooze button to set an interval
to bring back the reminder.

Task reminders are useful to automate tasks such as changing status, launching online meeting at a specific day and time. To set task reminders, do the following: Click displayed on the calendar Choose Tasks. Select the task from the drop-down. If you choose Call Customer, then enter the number of the customer you want to call. If you choose the Change Status task, then select the status you want to change to from the Select Status drop-down. If you choose Meeting task, then enter the meeting link. Set the date from the calendar Set the time for the task reminder. Enter location. Enter any additional notes. Click Add. The reminder is created, and it is displayed on the calendar (as a red bar). Note: You can edit the reminder by clicking the edit icon on the red bar before the expiry of the reminder date/time. You can also delete the

reminder by clicking the delete icon. At the configured date and time, a pop-up window appears to remind you of the task reminder. You can either click to accept the reminder or click the snooze button to set an interval to bring back the reminder. On accepting Call Customer task reminder, your status is changed to On Call and a call is made to the customer. On accepting the Change Status task reminder, your status is automatically changed by the system. On accepting the Meeting task reminder, an online meeting is launched by the system.
